REVIEWED_TREE: 5189480a28b1a31c06b8984dc8a3c3ae64bc0229 /home/user/.capy/work/wt-766
gstack: ok 1.92.19.0 for=review (behind=1 (latest: 1.92.20.0); fix: bash /home/user/.capy/drive/user-garry-tan/skills/gstack/scripts/install.sh --for review)

The range is three files. `lib/review-ledger.ts` (the negation filter `asserted()` in `parseFindings`) and the changelog fragment got a full read. I reviewed `test/review-dispatch.test.ts` in summary mode only: it adds 25 lines, one test for the GEVA-92 fix-check#5 negated forms, and I didn't pull in its payload text. `bun test test/review-dispatch.test.ts` passes at this tree (40 pass, 0 fail). I checked the cases below with a scratch probe that called `parseFindings` directly.

1. Unformatted prose findings whose only severity word follows a negation are now dropped silently (lib/review-ledger.ts:97). NEGATED only checks the word right before the label, so it also catches phrases that state a severity rather than deny one. On this tree, `This is no Low-severity issue: concurrent writes drop rows silently.` gives `[]`, and `- The limiter has no HIGH watermark, so the queue grows without bound.` also gives `[]`. Before the change, both were collected. This goes against the parser's own rule that losing a finding costs more than keeping a phantom one. The loss happens only when the line has no file:line and the reader leaves out its `Severity:` field line. When that field line is present, the META path still opens the finding with the earlier line as its head. INVESTIGATE: decide whether a negated label on a line with no location should fall back to the strongest label instead of nothing, at least for prose voices. Severity: Medium Blocks: no

2. A reply that only says it found nothing, with no clean marker, is now marked as not a review (lib/review-ledger.ts:188). For example, a fix-check reply ending `found nothing CRITICAL.` with no `NO FINDINGS` line now parses to zero findings, so `collect` records `review: false`. Before, it recorded a phantom CRITICAL. This fails closed, which is safer than a phantom blocker, but the symptom changes from a stuck review loop to missing coverage or a redispatch. INVESTIGATE: confirm that /ship handles `review: false` from fix-check without burning a review pass, and that the GEVA-92 reply carried `NO FINDINGS`. Severity: Low Blocks: no

3. A comma ends the negation, so a negated list still leaves a phantom finding (lib/review-ledger.ts:68). On this tree, `Found no new Critical, High issues.` gives a High finding. In the same way, `- Not Critical: …` is kept as Critical because the colon after the label counts as a field opener. Commit cc55f44 chose this conservative behavior on purpose, and the judge can't drop either finding, so a phantom can still use up a review pass. Neither phantom blocks at the floor unless it reads as CRITICAL. FIXABLE: carry the negation across a comma when the next label is directly followed by a plural noun such as "issues" or "findings". Severity: Low Blocks: no

4. The negation check takes quadratic time on a line full of labels (lib/review-ledger.ts:101). `asserted()` re-slices the prefix, strips its Markdown and runs NEGATED over it once per label. Measured on this tree: 8,000 labels on a 40 KB line took 33 ms, and 32,000 labels on a 160 KB line took 393 ms. The old code was linear. Normal reader output is far below this, so the risk is only a pasted blob. FIXABLE: test NEGATED against at most the last ~40 characters before the label. Severity: Low Blocks: no

5. The changelog doesn't fully describe the code (changelog.d/gst-766-collector-negated-labels.md:1). It lists "new", "remaining" and "other" as the optional words, but NEGATED also accepts "further", "additional" and "more". It mentions "or" but not "nor". FIXABLE: update the fragment to match. Severity: Low Blocks: no

Recommendation: Ship as-is because the strongest finding, unlocated prose like "no Low-severity issue" being dropped, only loses a finding when the reader also leaves out the Severity field its brief requires.
